193	:func:`advance_headers` durably checkpoints a verified header-page batch to
194	``path``. The file is one compact UTF-8 JSON document (non-ASCII written
195	unescaped, one trailing newline) with the exact top-level key order
196	``v, generation, anchor, tip, finalized, steps, hash``: ``v`` is 3
197	(version-1 and version-2 files are still read), ``generation`` is a
198	non-boolean positive integer incremented once per successful advance,
199	reorg or finalization, ``anchor`` is the first batch's pinned
200	``{height, block_hash}`` anchor (key order ``height, block_hash``), ``tip``
201	is the latest chain descriptor S, ``finalized`` is the irreversible
202	finality boundary as ``{height, block_hash}`` (version-1/version-2 files
203	are read with ``finalized`` equal to their ``anchor`` and migrated to
204	version 3 on the next successful write), ``steps`` is a non-empty array
205	of ``{kind, tip_hash, trust, documents, locators}`` items (one per
206	advance or reorg, nested key orders unchanged; ``kind`` is ``linear`` for
207	an :func:`advance_headers` step, which carries ``locators: null``, and
208	``locator`` for a :func:`reorg_headers` step, which carries the request
209	locators; version-1 ``{tip_hash, trust, documents}`` steps read as
210	``linear``) and ``hash`` is the SHA-256 of the canonical (sorted,
211	compact) JSON of the document with ``hash`` removed; version 3 keeps the
212	version-2 hash computation and serialization, extended by the one
213	``finalized`` field. The first use of ``path`` requires a legal
214	``anchor``; later advances accept ``None`` (continue from the stored tip)
215	or the stored tip's ``{height, block_hash}``. Verification itself is
216	:func:`verify_header_pages` unchanged against the caller-pinned
217	``tip_hash``. The new tip may never drop in height; at the same height
218	only the same ``block_hash`` moving from ``pending`` to ``confirmed`` is
219	accepted — anything else is an ``integrity`` failure. Re-submitting the
220	exact last batch (same ``tip_hash``, ``trust`` and ``documents``) is
221	idempotent: it verifies but neither bumps the generation nor touches the
222	file. Loading strictly replays every stored step (shape, hash, per-batch
223	verification and tip monotonicity), re-verifies that the stored
224	``finalized`` boundary belongs to the replayed branch — it must name the
225	anchor or a confirmed replayed header — and checks the stored tip; any
226	mismatch is a ``state`` failure and the file is never truncated or
227	rebuilt. Same-path advances, reorgs and finalizations share one lock and
228	the new file is atomically replaced into place; a failed write restores
229	the original bytes. Success returns ``{"ok": True, "generation",
230	"tip"}``; failure returns only ``{"ok": False, "error": category}`` with
231	category one of ``input/auth/integrity/state/io`` and nothing is raised.
232	
233	:func:`reorg_headers` durably checkpoints a verified locator-page batch — a
234	chain reorganization — to the same checkpoint file. The batch is verified
235	with :func:`verify_header_locator_pages` against the caller's ``locators``
236	and pinned ``tip_hash``; the checkpoint at ``path`` must already exist (a
237	missing file is ``io``). The reorg boundary is the closing tip of the last
238	stored step matching the batch's anchor, or the checkpoint's initial anchor
239	when no step matches (a batch anchoring anywhere else is an ``integrity``
240	failure); the boundary must also be the stored ``finalized`` boundary or a
241	branch point at or after it — a batch that would rewrite finalized history
242	is an ``integrity`` failure that leaves the file bytes and generation
243	untouched. Every step after the boundary is dropped, the new ``locator``
244	step is appended and ``replaced`` reports the dropped count. The new tip
245	may never drop below the stored tip's height; at the same height a
246	different ``block_hash`` — the reorganization itself — is accepted in
247	either status, while the same hash may only move from ``pending`` to
248	``confirmed``; anything else is an ``integrity`` failure. Re-submitting the
249	exact last locator step (same ``tip_hash``, ``trust``, ``documents`` and
250	``locators``) is idempotent: it returns the current generation with
251	``replaced: 0`` and neither bumps the generation nor touches the file.
252	Success returns ``{"ok": True, "generation", "tip", "replaced"}`` in that
253	key order; failure returns only ``{"ok": False, "error": category}`` with
254	category one of ``input`` (bad arguments or locator/batch shape), ``auth``
255	(signer version or signature), ``integrity`` (finality, boundary, chain,

257	its key-order, type, hash or replay checks, including finalized-boundary

261	:func:`finalize_headers` advances the irreversible finality boundary of a
262	checkpoint written by :func:`advance_headers` or :func:`reorg_headers`.
263	``finalize_headers(path, height, block_hash)`` takes no default arguments:
264	``path`` is a non-empty string, ``height`` a non-boolean non-negative

273	``finalized``; resubmitting the exact current boundary is idempotent — it
274	returns the current generation with the file bytes untouched. Success
275	returns ``{"ok": True, "generation", "finalized"}`` in that key order with
276	``finalized`` the closed ``{height, block_hash}`` document (key order
277	``height, block_hash``); failure returns only ``{"ok": False, "error":
278	category}`` with category one of ``input`` (bad arguments), ``integrity``
279	(the target is unknown, pending, past the tip, or moves the boundary
280	backwards or sideways), ``state`` (the checkpoint fails its parse,
281	key-order, digest, ownership or replay checks) and ``io`` (the checkpoint
282	is missing or cannot be read or written); nothing is raised.

284	:func:`apply_finality` applies a signed ``GET /v1/chain/finality``
285	credential to a checkpoint written by :func:`advance_headers` or
286	:func:`reorg_headers`. ``apply_finality(path, document, trust)`` takes no

288	the decoded response with the exact top-level key order
289	``finalized, tip, auth`` — ``finalized`` a closed ``{height, block_hash}``

291	chain descriptor S and ``auth`` ``{key_version, signature}`` (a

298	key version or a failed Ed25519 verification over
299	``SHA256(UTF8("ledger-finality-v1") || canonical_json(document without

304	sideways (a mismatched tip, an unknown, pending or dropped-fork target,
305	or a regressing boundary is ``integrity``). Applying the exact stored
306	boundary is idempotent — it returns the current generation and leaves
307	the file bytes untouched; raising the boundary increments the
308	generation once and atomically rewrites the file in the version-3
309	format (same serialization and hash rules as
310	:func:`finalize_headers`). Success returns
311	``{"ok": True, "generation", "finalized"}`` in that key order; failure
312	returns only ``{"ok": False, "error": category}`` and nothing is raised;
313	a failed application never changes the file bytes.
314	
315	:func:`header_locators` derives a fork-location locator request from a
316	checkpoint written by :func:`advance_headers` or :func:`reorg_headers`. The
317	file is strictly
318	reloaded and replayed under the same rules (never rewritten); the replayed
319	history yields the sequence B — the initial anchor and every step's closing
320	tip, ascending, with adjacent equal ``(height, block_hash)`` pairs
321	collapsed — and the request's locators walk B newest-first: up to ten

332	
333	:func:`advance` durably checkpoints a verified batch to ``path``. The
334	checkpoint file is one compact UTF-8 JSON document with the exact declared key
335	order ``generation, anchor, tip, context, state_hash`` and a single trailing
336	newline (non-ASCII written unescaped); ``generation`` starts at 1 and
337	increments per successful advance, ``anchor``/``tip`` are the batch's pinned
338	anchor and closed tip, ``context`` has the exact key order
339	``verified_at, trust, documents, verified_tx_ids`` (the ``now`` at verification,

344	Verification itself is :func:`verify_range_exports` unchanged. Same-path
345	advances share one lock and the new file is atomically replaced into place; a
346	failed verification never bumps the generation. An existing checkpoint is
347	strictly reloaded (key order, types, state hash and a context replay at its
348	``verified_at``); any mismatch is a ``state`` failure and the file is never
349	truncated or rebuilt. Failures return only ``{"ok": False, "error":
350	category}`` with category one of
351	``input/auth/expired/integrity/state/io``; success appends the new
352	``generation`` as the final result key.
353	
354	Every successful :func:`advance` also maintains a generation-history sidecar
355	at ``path + ".history"``: one compact UTF-8 JSON document (same serialization
356	rules as the checkpoint) with the exact top-level key order
357	``v, base, records, head``. ``v`` is 1; ``base`` is ``{generation, hash}``
358	naming the generation *before* the first retained record; each record is
359	``{checkpoint, prev, hash}`` where ``checkpoint`` is the persisted five-key
360	checkpoint document, ``prev`` is the previous record's hash (the first
361	record's is ``base.hash``) and ``hash`` is
362	``SHA256(ASCII(prev) || canonical_json(checkpoint))``; ``head`` is the last
363	record's hash. Record generations run consecutively from
364	``base.generation + 1``. A fresh path starts from ``base = {0, Z}`` (Z = 64
365	zeros); a pre-existing generation-``g`` checkpoint without a sidecar is
366	treated as ``base = {g-1, Z}`` with that checkpoint as the first record, and
367	later advances append. Both files are written under the same per-path lock as
368	one transaction: an ``io`` failure restores the original bytes best-effort
369	(a failed compensation surfaces as ``state`` on the next read); crash
370	atomicity across the two files is not guaranteed.
371	
372	:func:`history` reads (and prunes) the sidecar. ``history(path)`` returns
373	``{"ok", "base", "record", "head", "kept"}`` with ``record`` the last
374	generation's record and ``kept`` null; ``generation=`` selects one retained
375	generation (an absent one is a ``state`` failure). ``keep=n`` (mutually
376	exclusive with ``generation``; both must be non-boolean positive integers)
377	retains only the last ``min(n, count)`` records: when nothing is pruned the
378	file's bytes are untouched, otherwise ``base`` becomes the last pruned
379	record's ``{generation, hash}`` and the sidecar is rewritten (the checkpoint
380	file itself never changes). Loading replays every retained generation —
381	shape, state hash, context replay and anchor continuity — so any tampering
382	is a ``state`` failure; a missing or unreadable sidecar is ``io``.
383	
384	:func:`export_history` exports the retained sidecar pages as signed,
385	offline-verifiable page documents. ``export_history(path, key, after=None,

387	sidecar under the shared per-path lock and returns one page with the exact key
388	order ``base, records, next, head, checkpoint, auth``: ``base``/``records``
389	are the sidecar's own documents (nested key orders unchanged), ``head`` the
390	sidecar head, ``checkpoint`` the persisted five-key checkpoint (identical to
391	the last retained record's), ``next`` the page's last record generation when
392	another page follows or ``null`` on the final page, and ``auth`` is
393	``{public_key, signature}`` where the Ed25519 signature is made by the 64-hex
394	seed ``key`` over the SHA-256 of the canonical (sorted, compact,
395	unescaped-non-ASCII) JSON of the page with ``auth`` removed. ``after`` is
396	``None`` (start after ``base``) or a non-boolean non-negative integer naming
397	either ``base.generation`` or a non-last retained generation; ``limit`` is a
398	non-boolean integer in 1..200. Bad arguments are ``input``, a missing or
399	unreadable file ``io`` and a corrupt checkpoint/sidecar or unmatched cursor
400	``state``. With ``trust_path`` set to a signer log (see
401	:func:`history_trust`), the log is strictly loaded first (a missing log is
402	``io`` and a corrupt one ``state``) and the page is truncated to the longest
403	prefix, starting at the cursor, whose checkpoints all carry the same key
404	active at their ``verified_at``: it stops just before the first record that
405	would straddle an authorization boundary and sets ``next`` (non-null) so the
406	following page continues there. The seed ``key`` must derive to the public
407	key covering that whole span — an unknown or revoked covering key is an
408	``auth`` failure. A page ending exactly at the retained tail still closes
409	with ``next: null``.
410	
411	:func:`verify_history` verifies an ordered, non-empty list of such pages
412	offline against one pinned 64-hex Ed25519 ``public_key``. Every page must have
413	the exact key order and nested types; ``base``, ``head``, ``checkpoint`` and
414	the signing public key must be identical on every page; each Ed25519 signature
415	must verify over the auth-less canonical page digest. Records must run
416	consecutively from ``base.generation + 1`` and link across page seams through
417	each page's ``next`` (a non-final page's ``next`` is its last record
418	generation), every record hash is recomputed and every checkpoint is replayed
419	(state hash plus the stored batch context) with anchor continuity. The final
420	page alone carries ``next: null``, its last record's hash must equal ``head``
421	and its checkpoint must equal the page checkpoint; missing, duplicate or
422	reordered pages and any tampering are rejected. Success is ``{"ok": True}``;
423	failure is ``{"ok": False, "error": category}`` with category one of
424	``input`` (structure/types), ``auth`` (pinned key or signature) and
425	``integrity`` (chaining, pagination or checkpoint replay); nothing is raised.
426	
427	:func:`verify_history_trust` verifies the same pages against a signer
428	rotation/revocation log instead of one pinned page key, so each page's
429	``auth.public_key`` may differ. The ``trust`` document has the exact key
430	order ``root, records, head``: ``root`` is a 64-hex Ed25519 key that must
431	equal the pinned ``root`` argument; every non-empty record has the exact key
432	order ``at, key, status, prev, signature`` with ``at`` a plain
433	(non-boolean) positive strictly-ascending integer, ``key``/``prev`` 64
434	lowercase hex, ``status`` exactly ``active``/``revoked`` and ``signature``
435	128 lowercase hex. The first ``prev`` is 64 zeros, every later one is the

437	hash; each certificate is the root key's Ed25519 signature over the
438	SHA-256 of the record's canonical JSON with ``signature`` removed. An
439	``active`` record authorizes ``key`` from its ``at`` until the next record;
440	a ``revoked`` one withdraws it until a later ``active``. A page must name
441	the single key active at every checkpoint ``verified_at`` it carries — a
442	page straddling an authorization boundary is rejected — and its signature

444	chaining, pagination and checkpoint-replay rules stay identical to

449	record/pagination/checkpoint-replay defect); nothing is raised and success
450	is ``{"ok": True}``.

452	:func:`history_trust` persists such a signer log at its own file path.

465	newline serialization and atomic per-path-locked replace as the checkpoint

530	def canonical_bundle_bytes(bundle: dict) -> bytes:
531	    """Sorted, compact UTF-8 JSON of the bundle with its signature removed.
532	
533	    This is the exact byte document whose SHA-256 the source signs, so signers
534	    and verifiers always agree regardless of incoming key order. The
535	    serialization mirrors :func:`ledger.crypto.canonical_message`: sorted keys,
536	    compact separators, UTF-8 bytes.
537	    """
538	    unsigned = {key: value for key, value in bundle.items() if key != "signature"}
539	    return json.dumps(
540	        unsigned, sort_keys=True, separators=(",", ":")
541	    ).encode("utf-8")

545	    """The 32-byte SHA-256 digest covered by a bundle Ed25519 signature."""
546	    return hashlib.sha256(canonical_bundle_bytes(bundle)).digest()

549	def verify_bundle(bundle: object, trust: object, now: float | None = None) -> dict:
550	    """Verify an offline proof bundle against the local trust document.
551	
552	    Returns ``{"ok": True, "source": ..., "S": ..., "verified_tx_ids": [...]}``
553	    on success — extended bundles also carry ``"verified_accounts"`` — or
554	    ``{"ok": False, "error": category}`` on failure. Never raises for
555	    malformed input: every defect maps to one of the five categories.
556	    """
557	    current = time.time() if now is None else now
558	    try:
559	        source, candidate = _validate_inputs(bundle, trust)
560	        _authenticate(bundle, trust, source, current)
561	        blocks_raw = candidate["blocks"] if isinstance(candidate, dict) else candidate
562	        blocks = _recompute_chain(blocks_raw, trust)
563	        descriptor = _tip_descriptor(blocks)
564	        _check_candidate_summary(candidate, descriptor)
565	        _check_response(bundle["response"], descriptor)
566	        has_state = "state_root" in bundle
567	        if has_state:
568	            _check_state_anchor(bundle, blocks)
569	        verified_ids = _verify_proofs(bundle["proofs"], blocks)
570	        verified_accounts = (

583	        "verified_tx_ids": verified_ids,

593	def _validate_inputs(bundle: object, trust: object) -> tuple[str, object]:
594	    """Structural validation of bundle and trust.
595	
596	    Returns ``(source, candidate)`` where ``candidate`` is the raw candidate
597	    value (a bare block list or an export-format object carrying ``blocks``).
598	    The bundle itself is never mutated: the signature covers it verbatim.
599	    """
600	    if not isinstance(bundle, dict):
601	        raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
602	    for field in ("source", "expires_at", "response", "candidate", "proofs"):
603	        if field not in bundle:
604	            raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
605	    source = bundle["source"]
606	    if not isinstance(source, str) or not source:
607	        raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
608	    if not _is_int(bundle["expires_at"]):
609	        raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
610	    # The response is itself a JSON object; anything else cannot be checked
611	    # against the recomputed chain descriptor.
612	    if not isinstance(bundle["response"], dict):
613	        raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
614	    candidate = bundle["candidate"]
615	    blocks_raw = candidate.get("blocks") if isinstance(candidate, dict) else candidate
616	    if not isinstance(blocks_raw, list) or not blocks_raw:
617	        raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
618	    if not isinstance(bundle["proofs"], list):
619	        raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
620	    signature = bundle.get("signature")
621	    if signature is not None and (not isinstance(signature, str) or not signature):
622	        raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
623	    _validate_state_fields(bundle)
624	
625	    if not isinstance(trust, dict):
626	        raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
627	    if not crypto.is_hex64(trust.get("genesis_hash")):
628	        raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
629	    sources = trust.get("sources", {})
630	    if not isinstance(sources, dict):
631	        raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
632	    for name, entry in sources.items():
633	        if not isinstance(name, str) or not name or not isinstance(entry, dict):
634	            raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
635	        if not _is_int(entry.get("expires_at")):
636	            raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
637	        public_key = entry.get("public_key")
638	        # Ed25519 public keys are 32 raw bytes, i.e. 64 hex characters.
639	        if not isinstance(public_key, str) or not _HEX32_RE.fullmatch(public_key):
640	            raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
641	    allowlist = trust.get("allowlist", {})
642	    if not isinstance(allowlist, dict):
643	        raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
644	    for name, expires_at in allowlist.items():
645	        if not isinstance(name, str) or not name or not _is_int(expires_at):
646	            raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
647	    return source, candidate

650	def _validate_state_fields(bundle: dict) -> None:
651	    """Structural validation of the optional account-state extension.
652	
653	    The four state fields are all-or-nothing; when present, ``state_root`` and
654	    ``state_block_hash`` must be 64-char lowercase hex, ``state_height`` a
655	    non-boolean non-negative integer and ``state_proofs`` a non-empty list.
656	    Every item must carry exactly ``{height, proof}`` and every proof document
657	    exactly the eight documented keys with the right JSON types. Only shape
658	    and type are judged here — domain defects (bad hex, negative balances,
659	    illegal directions) are reported later as integrity/proof failures.
660	    """
661	    present = [field for field in STATE_FIELDS if field in bundle]
662	    if not present:
663	        return
664	    if len(present) != len(STATE_FIELDS):
665	        raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
666	    if not crypto.is_hex64(bundle["state_root"]):
667	        raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
668	    if not _is_int(bundle["state_height"]) or bundle["state_height"] < 0:
669	        raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
670	    if not crypto.is_hex64(bundle["state_block_hash"]):
671	        raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
672	    state_proofs = bundle["state_proofs"]
673	    if not isinstance(state_proofs, list) or not state_proofs:
674	        raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
675	    for item in state_proofs:
676	        if not isinstance(item, dict) or set(item) != {"height", "proof"}:
677	            raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
678	        if not _is_int(item["height"]):
679	            raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
680	        proof = item["proof"]
681	        if not isinstance(proof, dict) or set(proof) != _STATE_PROOF_KEYS:
682	            raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
683	        if not isinstance(proof["account"], str) or not proof["account"]:
684	            raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
685	        if not _is_int(proof["balance"]):
686	            raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
687	        transactions = proof["confirmed_transactions"]
688	        if not isinstance(transactions, list) or any(
689	            not isinstance(tx_id, str) for tx_id in transactions
690	        ):
691	            raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
692	        if not _is_int(proof["index"]):
693	            raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
694	        if not isinstance(proof["state_root"], str):
695	            raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
696	        if not _is_int(proof["height"]):
697	            raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
698	        if not isinstance(proof["block_hash"], str):
699	            raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
700	        if not isinstance(proof["siblings"], list):
701	            raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)

707	def _authenticate(
708	    bundle: dict, trust: dict, source: str, now: float
709	) -> None:
710	    """Check source trust, every deadline and the optional Ed25519 signature."""
711	    sources = trust.get("sources", {})
712	    allowlist = trust.get("allowlist", {})
713	    source_entry = sources.get(source)
714	    allowlist_expiry = allowlist.get(source)
715	    if source_entry is None and allowlist_expiry is None:
716	        raise _Failure(ERR_AUTH)
717	
718	    # All deadlines are checked before any signature work: an expired,
719	    # correctly-signed bundle is still unusable. A source listed in both
720	    # ``sources`` and ``allowlist`` is bound by both deadlines.
721	    if bundle["expires_at"] <= now:
722	        raise _Failure(ERR_EXPIRED)
723	    if source_entry is not None and source_entry["expires_at"] <= now:
724	        raise _Failure(ERR_EXPIRED)
725	    if allowlist_expiry is not None and allowlist_expiry <= now:
726	        raise _Failure(ERR_EXPIRED)
727	
728	    public_key = source_entry.get("public_key") if source_entry else None
729	    signature = bundle.get("signature")
730	    if public_key is not None:
731	        # A keyed source must sign: a missing signature cannot authenticate.
732	        if signature is None:
733	            raise _Failure(ERR_AUTH)
734	        if not crypto.verify_signature(
735	            public_key, bundle_signing_digest(bundle), signature
736	        ):
737	            raise _Failure(ERR_INTEGRITY)
738	        return
739	    # The source reached this point only through the allowlist (every sources
740	    # entry pins a key). An unsigned allowlisted bundle is therefore accepted;
741	    # a signature with no pinned key to check it against is meaningless.
742	    if signature is not None:
743	        raise _Failure(ERR_AUTH)

759	def _recompute_chain(candidate_raw: list, trust: dict) -> list[Block]:
760	    """Recompute and validate the whole candidate chain from the pinned genesis.
761	
762	    Mirrors the node's own candidate rules except the endowment balance replay
763	    (an offline client holds no balance convention): genesis anchor, heights,
764	    prev_hash linkage, per-transaction tx_id and Ed25519 signatures, unique
765	    tx_id-sorted transactions, Merkle roots, block hashes and the
766	    pending-only-at-tip rule. Every field is checked on the *raw* JSON value so
767	    coercions such as ``"1"`` or ``1.0`` heights are rejected outright; such
768	    type/domain defects (non-integer or negative height, non-positive or
769	    non-integer amount) are reported as ``input``, while recomputation
770	    mismatches stay ``integrity``.
771	    """
772	    blocks: list[Block] = []
773	    seen_tx_ids: set[str] = set()
774	    for position, block_raw in enumerate(candidate_raw):
775	        if not isinstance(block_raw, dict):
776	            raise _Failure(ERR_INTEGRITY)
777	        height = block_raw.get("height")
778	        prev_hash = block_raw.get("prev_hash")
779	        merkle_root = block_raw.get("merkle_root")
780	        block_hash = block_raw.get("block_hash")
781	        status = block_raw.get("status")
782	        txs_raw = block_raw.get("transactions")
783	        # A height of the wrong type or sign is a field-type defect (input),
784	        # not a chain mismatch: strings, floats and booleans must never be
785	        # coerced into plausible integers before the linkage checks below.
786	        if not _is_int(height) or height < 0:
787	            raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
788	        if not isinstance(prev_hash, str):
789	            raise _Failure(ERR_INTEGRITY)
790	        if not crypto.is_hex64(merkle_root) or not crypto.is_hex64(block_hash):
791	            raise _Failure(ERR_INTEGRITY)
792	        if status not in ("pending", "confirmed") or not isinstance(txs_raw, list):
793	            raise _Failure(ERR_INTEGRITY)
794	        if height != position:
795	            raise _Failure(ERR_INTEGRITY)
796	        expected_prev = (
797	            GENESIS_PREV_HASH if position == 0 else blocks[position - 1].block_hash
798	        )
799	        if prev_hash != expected_prev:
800	            raise _Failure(ERR_INTEGRITY)
801	        if position == 0:
802	            # Genesis must be the exact block the client pinned: confirmed,
803	            # empty, and carrying the trusted hash (recomputed below too).
804	            if status != STATUS_CONFIRMED or txs_raw:
805	                raise _Failure(ERR_INTEGRITY)
806	            if block_hash != trust["genesis_hash"]:
807	                raise _Failure(ERR_INTEGRITY)
808	        elif position < len(candidate_raw) - 1 and status != STATUS_CONFIRMED:
809	            # A pending block may only sit at the chain tip.
810	            raise _Failure(ERR_INTEGRITY)
811	
812	        tx_ids: list[str] = []
813	        for raw_tx in txs_raw:
814	            if not isinstance(raw_tx, dict):
815	                raise _Failure(ERR_INTEGRITY)
816	            sender = raw_tx.get("from")
817	            recipient = raw_tx.get("to")
818	            amount = raw_tx.get("amount")
819	            signature = raw_tx.get("signature")
820	            stored_tx_id = raw_tx.get("tx_id")
821	            if not isinstance(sender, str) or not sender:
822	                raise _Failure(ERR_INTEGRITY)
823	            if not isinstance(recipient, str) or not recipient:
824	                raise _Failure(ERR_INTEGRITY)
825	            # Same rule as the block height: the raw amount must already be a
826	            # non-boolean positive integer — never a coercible string, float
827	            # or bool — so a domain/type defect is reported as input.
828	            if not _is_int(amount) or amount <= 0:
829	                raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
830	            if not isinstance(signature, str) or not signature:
831	                raise _Failure(ERR_INTEGRITY)
832	            message = crypto.canonical_message(sender, recipient, amount)
833	            tx_id = crypto.compute_tx_id(message)
834	            if stored_tx_id != tx_id or not crypto.is_hex64(stored_tx_id):
835	                raise _Failure(ERR_INTEGRITY)
836	            if not crypto.verify_signature(sender, message, signature):
837	                raise _Failure(ERR_INTEGRITY)
838	            if tx_id in seen_tx_ids:
839	                raise _Failure(ERR_INTEGRITY)
840	            seen_tx_ids.add(tx_id)
841	            tx_ids.append(tx_id)
842	        if tx_ids != sorted(tx_ids):
843	            raise _Failure(ERR_INTEGRITY)
844	        if crypto.merkle_root(tx_ids) != merkle_root:
845	            raise _Failure(ERR_INTEGRITY)
846	        recomputed = compute_block_hash(height, prev_hash, merkle_root)
847	        if recomputed != block_hash:
848	            raise _Failure(ERR_INTEGRITY)
849	        # Parsed only after every raw field has checked out; never trusted for
850	        # the comparison decisions above.
851	        try:
852	            blocks.append(Block.from_dict(block_raw))
853	        except (KeyError, TypeError, ValueError):
854	            raise _Failure(ERR_INTEGRITY) from None
855	    return blocks

888	def _check_state_anchor(bundle: dict, blocks: list[Block]) -> None:
889	    """Bind the state extension's anchor to the recomputed candidate chain.
890	
891	    ``state_height`` must name a confirmed candidate block whose hash equals
892	    ``state_block_hash``; an unknown height, a pending block or a hash
893	    mismatch is an integrity failure. Every state-proof item and document

909	        if proof["state_root"] != state_root or proof["block_hash"] != block_hash:
910	            raise _Failure(ERR_INTEGRITY)

915	
916	def _verify_proofs(proofs_raw: list, blocks: list[Block]) -> list[str]:
917	    """Validate uniqueness and cross-block consistency of every proof.
918	
919	    Each entry is ``{"height": int, "proof": doc}`` and the proof document
920	    follows the server shape ``{height, tx_id, index, merkle_root, block_hash,
921	    siblings}``. Proofs for the pending tip are forbidden. The verified
922	    transaction ids are returned sorted ascending.
923	    """
924	    verified: list[str] = []
925	    seen: set[tuple] = set()
926	    for item in proofs_raw:
927	        if not isinstance(item, dict):
928	            raise _Failure(ERR_PROOF)
929	        height = item.get("height")
930	        proof = item.get("proof")
931	        if not _is_int(height) or not isinstance(proof, dict):
932	            raise _Failure(ERR_PROOF)
933	        if height < 0 or height >= len(blocks):
934	            raise _Failure(ERR_PROOF)
935	        block = blocks[height]
936	        if block.height != height:
937	            raise _Failure(ERR_PROOF)
938	        # Pending tips never carry trustworthy proofs.
939	        if block.status != STATUS_CONFIRMED:
940	            raise _Failure(ERR_PROOF)
941	
942	        tx_id = proof.get("tx_id")
943	        index = proof.get("index")
944	        if not crypto.is_hex64(tx_id) or not _is_int(index):
945	            raise _Failure(ERR_PROOF)
946	        # The item height and the proof document's own fields must agree with
947	        # the candidate block they claim inclusion in.
948	        if proof.get("height") != height or proof.get("block_hash") != block.block_hash:
949	            raise _Failure(ERR_PROOF)
950	        if proof.get("merkle_root") != block.merkle_root:
951	            raise _Failure(ERR_PROOF)
952	        if index < 0 or index >= len(block.transactions):
953	            raise _Failure(ERR_PROOF)
954	        if block.transactions[index].tx_id != tx_id:
955	            raise _Failure(ERR_PROOF)
956	
957	        key = (height, tx_id)
958	        if key in seen:
959	            raise _Failure(ERR_PROOF)
960	        seen.add(key)
961	
962	        if not crypto.verify_merkle_proof(
963	            tx_id,
964	            proof.get("siblings"),
965	            block.merkle_root,
966	            block.block_hash,
967	            block.block_hash,
968	        ):
969	            raise _Failure(ERR_PROOF)
970	        verified.append(tx_id)
971	    return sorted(verified)

974	def _verify_state_proofs(bundle: dict, blocks: list[Block]) -> list[str]:
975	    """Verify every account-state proof against the bundle's state anchor.
976	
977	    The anchor's confirmed transactions determine the ascending account set;
978	    each proof's ``account`` must belong to it and its ``index`` must be the
979	    account's position in that ordering. ``height`` + ``account`` pairs must
980	    be unique. Every proof is then checked with
981	    :func:`crypto.verify_account_proof` against the bundle's ``state_root``,
982	    ``state_height`` and ``state_block_hash``; any failure — an illegal
983	    direction or hash, a forged leaf, an illegal self-pair, a malformed
984	    sibling path — is a proof failure. Returns the verified accounts sorted
985	    ascending.
986	    """
987	    height = bundle["state_height"]
988	    # The account set of the anchor height: every account touched by a
989	    # confirmed transaction up to and including the anchor block, ascending.
990	    accounts: set[str] = set()
991	    for block in blocks[: height + 1]:
992	        if block.status != STATUS_CONFIRMED:
993	            continue
994	        for tx in block.transactions:
995	            accounts.add(tx.sender)
996	            accounts.add(tx.recipient)
997	    position = {account: index for index, account in enumerate(sorted(accounts))}
998	
999	    verified: list[str] = []
1000	    seen: set[tuple] = set()
1001	    for item in bundle["state_proofs"]:
1002	        proof = item["proof"]
1003	        account = proof["account"]
1004	        expected = position.get(account)
1005	        # An account outside the anchor's set, or an index that is not the
1006	        # account's ascending position (including out-of-range), is a proof
1007	        # failure.
1008	        if expected is None or proof["index"] != expected:
1009	            raise _Failure(ERR_PROOF)
1010	        key = (item["height"], account)
1011	        if key in seen:
1012	            raise _Failure(ERR_PROOF)
1013	        seen.add(key)
1014	        if not crypto.verify_account_proof(
1015	            proof,
1016	            bundle["state_root"],
1017	            height,
1018	            bundle["state_block_hash"],
1019	        ):
1020	            raise _Failure(ERR_PROOF)
1021	        verified.append(account)
1022	    return sorted(verified)

1336	def _authenticate_range_export(document: dict, trust: dict, now: float) -> None:
1337	    """Check mode-specific source authorization and every deadline.

1340	    carry ``attestation: null``. An ``attested`` export is authorized one of
1341	    two ways:
1342	
1343	    * the trust document carries a ``source_key_history`` mapping (the new
1344	      rule): the source must appear in the mapping — the historical public key
1345	      matching and signature verification happen by attestation version in
1346	      :func:`_verify_range_attestation`; the trust ``sources`` entry and its

1351	      ``sources`` entry whose unexpired deadline is checked.

1354	    correctly-signed export is still unusable.
1355	    """
1356	    source = document["source"]
1357	    mode = document["mode"]
1358	    sources = trust.get("sources", {})
1359	    allowlist = trust.get("allowlist", {})
1360	    if mode == "plain":
1361	        if source not in allowlist:
1362	            raise _Failure(ERR_AUTH)
1363	        # A plain export carrying an attestation is not a plain delivery.
1364	        if document["attestation"] is not None:
1365	            raise _Failure(ERR_AUTH)
1366	    elif _has_key_history(trust):
1367	        # Historical-key authorization: the source (and later the attestation
1368	        # version) must resolve in the mapping; the current registry entry is
1369	        # deliberately not consulted.
1370	        if source not in trust["source_key_history"]:
1371	            raise _Failure(ERR_AUTH)
1372	    elif source not in sources:
1373	        raise _Failure(ERR_AUTH)
1374	
1375	    if document["expires_at"] <= now:
1376	        raise _Failure(ERR_EXPIRED)
1377	    if mode == "plain":
1378	        if allowlist[source] <= now:
1379	            raise _Failure(ERR_EXPIRED)
